challenge.better_approach: Considered: dropping the settled-red skip for sieves, or for every proof on commit. Rejected: it re-runs every red on every commit (Law 1), and it puts no reason on the seal. Considered: putting every file a proof opens into its closure. Rejected: that reverses b7d5df9919fe clause 3. A declared SCANS is the smallest change that names a sieve's subject.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every sieve's subject can be written as repo-relative globs. Both tester sieves rglob a fixed pattern, and that is true for them. A sieve whose subject is computed at run time would not fit, and it would stay blind as it is today.
challenge.prior_art: In-house: b7d5df9919fe (PROVED) keeps fixture data reads out of the closure, clause 3; 6e50ed204abc and 734b22d09f2e widen the closure only to code executed; 675ab0daa171 narrows it to the import closure; 143e3974647b chooses which seals a commit re-runs. None declares a scanned folder. Grep of tickets/ and questions/ for fingerprint_closure plus scanned or settled-red found nothing that covers it.
challenge.real_collision: b7d5df9919fe clause 3. Its why is that a fixture's data is not the code under proof. A sieve's scanned folder IS the code under proof, so the two are distinct and the distinction is recorded: SCANS is declared, while a data read is not. That ticket's clause-3 proof staying green is a constraint of this one (cc_0 2026-11-20).

answers.falsifier: after a repair to a file a sieve scans, a commit's reseal re-runs that sieve and reports it resealed, not settled-red; a fixture data read (b7d5df9919fe clause 3) stays out of its proof's closure
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured at a land, not imagined: /var/tmp/proves/commitb.out on akiendelllinux records 'reseal: 3 settled-red' for two sieve proofs the build had repaired (wt-0dbb 8ab52a07a, wt-f92d b47a845c1)
answers.how: The proof declares a module-level SCANS list of repo-relative globs. The tester's seal reads it from the source (ast, no import), records it as evidence.scans and unions the matches into fingerprint_closure; validation_store.closure_of re-expands evidence.scans whenever it is read, so a file added later that matches moves the fingerprint too. The two tester sieves declare SCANS. A red-first proof seals a fixture sieve, edits and adds a scanned file, and reads the fingerprint move.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (a settled answer is not re-derived, so the fingerprint has to say what the answer was taken over) and Law 8 (a sealed red that cannot be cleared by the repair is a seal that does not measure its subject).
answers.what: A proof whose subject is a folder declares what it scans, and its seal's fingerprint covers what those globs match, so a repair to a scanned file moves the fingerprint and the commit's reseal re-runs the sieve instead of keeping its red as settled.

bullets.text: A sieve proof's seal is blind to the folder it scans: after a repair the reseal keeps its red as 'settled' (Law 1), and only naming the proof by hand clears it. Measured at 0dbb and f92d's lands 2026-11-20.
The fix keeps b7d5's rule (fixture data stays out of the closure) by making the subject declared: SCANS names it, and closure_of re-expands it on every read.
